hitEnd after a failed find (d15, 62.0 and 67.0, anonymous and @IsTest, two repeats): a failed unanchored find always
  reports hitEnd=true (also pattern_matcher R011 and d14_neg_lookahead_nomatch). A pattern anchored at the start makes one
  attempt: ^(a+)+b on 24 a gives hitEnd=true and on 23 a plus c gives false. The @IsTest rows were captured too; only
  the anonymous rows are in org.tsv.
  Java keeps its Start wrapper unless the root node is a bare ^: (^(a+)+b) and (?:^(a+)+b) on 23 a plus c give
  hitEnd=true. (?i)^(s+)+x on 20 s plus U+017F gives find=false hitEnd=false (ASCII-only fold without u).
  d15 anonymous and @IsTest rows: two repeats, 62.0 and 67.0, in org.tsv (classes Rxd150062 and Rxd150067).
(?x) rows d16 (62.0 and 67.0, anonymous and @IsTest, two repeats): a comment ends at \r and at U+2028 but, under d, only at \n;
  whitespace splits tokens: (?x)( ?:a) is a non-capturing group, (?x)\0 1 4 2 reads octal 142 and (?x)\x2 3 reads hex 23.
(?x) rows d17 (62.0 and 67.0, anonymous and @IsTest, two repeats): the character after (? is read raw, so (?x)(? =a)a is an Unknown inline modifier
  while (?x)(? :a) is a non-capturing group; ( ?<n>a)\k<n> compiles with 1 group; a comment inside a class ends at \r.
(?x) rows d17x_C01..C32 (62.0 and 67.0, @IsTest, two repeats; all four runs agree and equal the Java 21 predictions): classes Rxd17x0062 and Rxd17x0067
  are the research packet's RegexXTest with @IsTest added to the class and the reserved word end renamed. They show:
  the six whitespace characters skip; a comment ends at \n, \r (not under d), U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029, but Java returns U+0085, U+2028, U+2029
  and NUL as pattern characters; whitespace splits \0 \x \u payloads and counted repeats after the first digit; (? x) and (?-x ) are errors.
